Plan Load-Balanced SLURM Array Chunk Assignments

Source: R/utils.R
plan_chunks.Rd

Partitions n_tasks tasks across ceiling(n_tasks / chunk_size) SLURM array chunks using one of three strategies:

  • "contiguous": sequential contiguous slices (default).

  • "round_robin": interleaved modulo assignment, useful when tasks are ordered monotonically by problem size.

  • "lpt": Longest Processing Time first greedy load balancing using task_weights to minimize maximum chunk runtime (makespan) when tasks exhibit strong heterogeneity.

Usage

plan_chunks(
  n_tasks,
  chunk_size,
  strategy = c("contiguous", "round_robin", "lpt"),
  task_weights = NULL
)

Arguments

n_tasks

Positive integer total number of tasks.

chunk_size

Positive integer target tasks per chunk (sets total chunk count n_chunks = ceiling(n_tasks / chunk_size)).

strategy

Chunking strategy: "contiguous", "round_robin", or "lpt".

task_weights

Optional positive numeric vector of length n_tasks representing relative per-task cost or runtime (required for "lpt").

Value

A tibble::tibble() with one row per chunk containing chunk_id, start_task, end_task, n_tasks, task_indices (list-column), and estimated_weight.

Examples

weights <- c(100, 90, 80, 10, 10, 10, 5, 5)
plan_chunks(8L, chunk_size = 2L, strategy = "lpt", task_weights = weights)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 6
#>   chunk_id start_task end_task n_tasks task_indices estimated_weight
#>      <int>      <int>    <int>   <int> <list>                  <dbl>
#> 1        1          1        1       1 <int [1]>                 100
#> 2        2          2        2       1 <int [1]>                  90
#> 3        3          3        3       1 <int [1]>                  80
#> 4        4          4        8       5 <int [5]>                  40
